results.name: secondary-reboot
results.title: MLAG secondary reboot
results.action: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as secondary, and after a loss-free baseline reboots it with `/system reboot` (1 s delay). The runner waits for the guest uptime to reset, then keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: The MLAG primary keeps the shared system ID, so both traffic hosts keep their LACP partner and forward over their bond member to the primary, which delivers locally without the peer port. The virtual links keep carrier, so each host drops its member to the secondary only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: The rejoining secondary keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with the primary (mlag-init-delay, default 1 min), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The MLAG bonds client1 and client2 are edge ports and forward at once, so loss is brief or none.

results.name: primary-reboot
results.title: MLAG primary reboot
results.action: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as primary, and after a loss-free baseline reboots it with `/system reboot` (1 s delay). The runner waits for the guest uptime to reset, then keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

first_lines.line: <28>Nov 24 11:57:11 dc1-core-mlag2 bridge,warning MLAG: remote heartbeat timeout

phases.name: Primary down
phases.expected: The MLAG secondary reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID (mlag-lacp-fallback=yes) and both traffic hosts renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. The virtual links keep carrier, so each host drops its member to the primary only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). The secondary's edge MLAG bonds keep forwarding throughout.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: The rebooted peer keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID. Both traffic hosts renegotiate LACP to the shared system ID, with brief loss.
